areaDescription: Beneath the town’s oldest streets lie the Lower Vaults, a maze of sunken passages, forgotten cisterns, and half-collapsed chambers where damp stone sweats in the torchlight. Echoes linger too long here, and those who descend without purpose often return with empty purses, shaken nerves, or not at all.

map.notes: Extended schema with AI-friendly navigation fields

locations.name: Veiled Guild Hall
locations.description: A half-submerged guild chamber where Lower Vault descent crews are licensed, briefed, and quietly threatened into caution. Chalk sigils on the walls dampen echoes, while a sunken training floor demonstrates how to move through flooded corridors without disturbing ward-stones.

npcs.name: Letharel, the silent border warden
npcs.description: A clipped, observant warden who verifies descent permits and watches for anyone carrying surface relics without clearance.

npcs.name: Mirael, a surface-contact scout
npcs.description: A dust-streaked scout trading rumors, route notes, and whispered warnings about unstable passages below.

monsters.name: Echo-Haunt
monsters.description: A lingering psychic imprint in the guild's training floor that lashes out when old descent drills are spoken aloud.

plotHooks: A sealed route ledger mentions a recent unauthorized descent into the deepest vaults.
Mirael can point the party toward a safer approach if they agree to recover a lost signal mirror.
The guild's permit board includes a coded warning about a 'listening chamber' below.
locations.dmInstructions: Use this as the party's entry point into Lower Vault Descents. It should feel controlled, tense, and full of practical warnings rather than open hospitality. Letharel can redirect the party toward the Echoing Threshold Gate if they do not have a legitimate reason to descend.

doors.name: Front Archway
doors.description: A broad stone arch hung with damp curtains of treated hide that reduce echo and conceal movement.

doors.name: Permit Office Door
doors.description: A narrow iron-banded door leading to records and route maps, marked with chalk sigils.

traps.name: Echo Bell Wire
traps.damage: 2d6 thunder damage and alerts nearby vault sentries

dcChecks: Investigation DC 13: Notice the coded warning hidden among the descent permits.
Insight DC 12: Determine which guild member is hiding the most useful route information.
History DC 14: Recognize the oldest chalk marks as pre-Numillian descent notation.
locations.accessibility: Easy to find from the upper streets, though entry is controlled by guild authority and permit checks.

features.name: Echo-Damping Chalk
features.description: White geometric markings on the walls absorb sound and make whispered conversations oddly clear.

features.name: Floodline Stair
features.description: A stepped basin shows the safe water level for the lower passages and marks where recent flooding has risen.

features.name: Permit Board of Bone Slats
features.description: Descent licenses and warnings are pinned to pale slats, some of them altered in a hand that is not the guild's.

encounters.name: Permit Inspection
encounters.description: Letharel or a guild clerk questions the party's purpose, testing whether they are prepared for the vaults.

encounters.name: Collapsed Drill Test
encounters.description: A section of the training floor gives way into a shallow maintenance pit, forcing a quick response before anyone is pinned.

locations.adventureSummary: The Veiled Guild Hall is the controlled gateway into the Lower Vault Descents, where the party can gather warnings, secure access, and learn that something below has begun to listen back.

locations.name: Silent Watch Barracks
locations.description: A cramped barracks carved into older stonework, where wardens sleep in shifts beside polished shields and sealed helms. The air smells of oil, wet wool, and the faint copper tang of recent spellwork used to calm restless echoes.

npcs.name: Veyrun, a Wardkeeper captain
npcs.description: A disciplined captain who keeps the barracks in strict order and has begun rationing patrol routes due to unexplained losses below.

monsters.name: Vault Rat Swarm
monsters.description: A hungry swarm drawn to stored grain and the scent of old water, emboldened by the barracks' noise and heat.

monsters.name: Gray Echo
monsters.description: A pale, half-seen remnant of a fallen patrol member that repeats commands before striking from the dark.

plotHooks: A patrol board lists a missing watch team last seen near a cistern corridor.
Veyrun has notes about a phrase repeated by lost wardens: 'the vault remembers names.'
A locker contains a torn scrap from Kobe's hiding place, proving someone has been moving through the lower routes.
locations.dmInstructions: This location should be tense and martial, with the Wardkeepers trying to maintain order while clearly losing control of the lower levels. Veyrun can provide practical information but will not reveal everything unless convinced the party can help.

doors.name: Barracks Main Door
doors.description: A thick oak-and-iron door reinforced with a barred crossbeam and ward-chalk around the frame.

doors.name: Armory Hatch
doors.description: A low hatch of riveted iron leading to weapons storage and patrol gear.
doors.trap: A pressure rune releases a blinding flash of white-blue light.

traps.name: Alarm Rune Plate
traps.damage: 2d8 lightning damage and an alarm that summons nearby wardens

dcChecks: Perception DC 13: Hear the subtle scrape of something moving under the bunk platforms.
Investigation DC 14: Reconstruct the route of the missing patrol from stained floor marks and mud.
Persuasion DC 15: Convince Veyrun to share restricted patrol notes.
locations.accessibility: Accessible from the guild hall by permission or force; the wardens restrict casual entry.

features.name: Weapon Racks
features.description: Spears and shortbows are stacked in careful order, but several are missing matching arrows or spearheads.

features.name: Patrol Board
features.description: A slate board tracks shifts, missing personnel, and routes that end abruptly in red chalk.

features.name: Restless Bunks
features.description: The bunks shake faintly at night as if something below is moving in rhythm with the sleepers' breathing.

encounters.name: Barracks Drill Challenge
encounters.description: The wardens demand proof of competence before sharing sensitive information.

encounters.name: Night-Rattle Intrusion
encounters.description: A vault-born creature tests the barracks perimeter, forcing the party and wardens to defend the line.

locations.adventureSummary: The Silent Watch Barracks exposes the Lower Vaults' failing defenses, giving the party patrol intelligence, martial allies, and a direct clue that the missing people are connected to deeper psychic disturbances.

locations.name: Echoing Threshold Gate
locations.description: A narrow gatehouse where the stone itself seems tuned to carry whispers downward. The gate’s rune-etched lintel amplifies voices into layered echoes, making it hard to tell which words are spoken now and which are trapped in the masonry from years ago.

npcs.name: Thalanis, Secrecy Council examiner
npcs.description: A severe examiner evaluating whether the party should be allowed farther below, and whether they are a threat to Numillian's secrecy.

monsters.name: Resonant Sentinel
monsters.description: An animated ward construct that attacks anyone whose words fail the gate's verbal protocol.

plotHooks: The gate only opens cleanly when the party repeats a phrase heard from the barracks' missing patrol.
Thalanis carries information about a sealed chamber tied to the crisis, but only releases it if the party proves discretion.
A hidden slot in the gate frame contains a torn note naming Kobe and a 'transfer to the inner cisterns.'
locations.dmInstructions: This is a controlled checkpoint between the safer guild-managed lower routes and the more dangerous interior vaults. Make the gate feel like a legal, magical, and psychological threshold. Thalanis should challenge the party's motives and may delay access if they seem reckless.

doors.name: Threshold Portcullis
doors.description: A descending iron lattice etched with concentric ward rings and old repair welds.
doors.trap: If forced without the correct phrase, the gate releases a sonic pulse and seals for one round.

doors.name: Side Examiner Door
doors.description: A narrow stone door leading to the examiner's alcove and record niche, fitted flush into the wall.

traps.name: Sonic Rebound Rune
traps.damage: 3d6 thunder damage and disadvantage on the next Wisdom check due to disorientation

dcChecks: Arcana DC 15: Decode the verbal protocol required to keep the gate from triggering.
Insight DC 14: Tell that Thalanis is withholding a larger problem from the party.
Perception DC 15: Spot the hidden note lodged in the gate frame.
locations.accessibility: Requires authorization, persuasion, or stealth; the gate is heavily monitored and magically enforced.

features.name: Echo Lattice
features.description: Rings of carved stone cause every sound to return in a distorted chorus, complicating conversation and stealth.

features.name: Examiner's Niche
features.description: A small side alcove contains scroll tubes, verdict marks, and a ledger of who was allowed below.

features.name: Seal Glyphs
features.description: Blue-gray runes pulse faintly when lies are told nearby, making the gate feel accusatory.

encounters.name: Protocol Trial
encounters.description: Thalanis demands a spoken verification of intent and purpose before granting passage.

encounters.name: Ward Pulse Backlash
encounters.description: A failed attempt to force the gate awakens the sonic defenses and draws attention from below.

locations.adventureSummary: The Echoing Threshold Gate is the final controlled barrier before the deeper vaults, where legal scrutiny, magical wards, and hidden evidence all point toward an inner crisis the party can no longer ignore.

locations.name: Inner Seal Gate
locations.description: A massive inner gate set into a pressure-scarred wall, built to keep the oldest chambers sealed even if the lower town floods. Its central seal is cracked, and every few minutes a soft pulse ripples through the stone as though something on the other side is testing the lock from within.

npcs.name: Kobe, the life at the center of the crisis
npcs.description: A frightened but resilient resident who has become the focal point of the vault crisis, carrying memories and psychic residue that can stabilize or doom the wards below.
npcs.attitude: Terrified, exhausted, and pleading for help

monsters.name: Ward-Torn Horror
monsters.description: A warped guardian entity that leaks from the cracked seal when the gate is disturbed.

monsters.name: Drowned Memory
monsters.description: A psychic manifestation formed from flooded thoughts and old fear, attacking with waves of confusion and grief.

lootTable: Vault map scrap with a hidden route
plotHooks: Kobe can identify the source of the crisis and reveal who last moved them through the vaults.
The cracked seal matches markings found in the Echoing Threshold Gate, confirming the same force is destabilizing both barriers.
A hidden drain behind the gate leads toward the Sanctum of Shuluth, suggesting the crisis is being guided rather than accidental.
locations.dmInstructions: This is the most important location in Lower Vault Descents. Protect Kobe's significance and treat the gate as both a physical barrier and a psychic wound in the city. The party should learn that the crisis is personal, dangerous, and tied to the deeper Numillian plot without resolving the larger conflict here.

doors.name: Inner Seal Door
doors.description: A titanic slab of stone and bronze with a central locking disc split by age and pressure.
doors.trap: Breaking the seal without proper stabilization unleashes a psychic shockwave and partial flooding.

doors.name: Drain Access Panel
doors.description: A rusted maintenance panel set low in the wall, hidden behind mineral buildup and old ward paste.

traps.name: Psychic Seal Surge
traps.damage: 4d6 psychic damage and the target is stunned until the end of its next turn on a failed Wisdom save

dcChecks: Medicine DC 14: Stabilize Kobe long enough for them to speak clearly.
Arcana DC 17: Identify how the cracked seal is tied to psychic pressure rather than simple structural failure.
Survival DC 13: Track the path of recent movement through the flooded grit and identify who passed here last.
locations.accessibility: Locked behind the deepest lower routes; only reachable after navigating the guild hall, barracks, and threshold gate.

features.name: Cracked Central Seal
features.description: The gate's core binding is visibly fractured, leaking cold air and faint whispers from the sealed side.

features.name: Flood Basin
features.description: A shallow basin collects seepage and reflects distorted images of the party when the seal pulses.

features.name: Maintenance Drain
features.description: A narrow drain channel offers a hidden route onward and suggests the crisis has been deliberately bypassing the main defenses.

encounters.name: Seal Disturbance
encounters.description: Approaching the gate triggers waves of psychic static that can disorient the entire party.

encounters.name: Kobe's Collapse
encounters.description: At a critical moment, Kobe's panic or memory surge may trigger the gate's defenses, requiring the party to calm and protect them.

locations.adventureSummary: The Inner Seal Gate is the crisis point of the Lower Vault Descents, where Kobe's importance becomes undeniable and the party learns that the city's deepest defenses are failing under psychic pressure.
